2020
 In The Court Of Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma
 Principal District & Sessions Judge /
 Food Safety Appellate Tribunal
New Delhi

In the matter of :
Fsat No. 10/2018

Connaught Place,

 Date of filing of appeal : 12.09.2018
 Date of arguments : 15.10.2020

Date of judgment : 20.10.2020
Judgment
1.
Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose of the present appeal challenging the impugned order dated 02.08.2018, whereby the appellant was found guilty.

The Ld. Adjudicating Officer inter alia held that the appellant failed to discharge efficiently the social responsibility of providing wholesome and branded eatable items, which may have an adverse impact on the health of the customer.
The Ld. Adjudicating Officer imposed a penalty u/s 54 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short 'the FSS Act') upon the appellant.
2. In backdrop, on 14.10.2017, the FSO took a sample of approx. 2 kg of "Rasbhari" from an open tray having no label declaration.
The sample was taken under the direction and supervision of the Designated Officer Sh. Satish Kumar Gupta.
The sample was taken after proper cutting into smallest possible pieces with the help of clean and dry steel knife in a clean and dry tray and mixed with the same knife.
In each sample bottle, 40 drops of formalin were added.
The FBO declared that the "Rasbhari" was made from Chhena, Sugar and Arrowroot.
The FBO declared the same for sale for human consumption Sh

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The sample was sent to the Food Analyst.

The Food Analyst vide his report dated 17.10.2017 opined that the sample contains extraneous matter viz. added vegetable oil in contravention of Section 26(2)(ii) read with the definition of extraneous matter as defined u/s 3(1)(i) of the FSS Act,
2006.
4.

The FSO filed a complaint before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer for violation of provision of Section 26(1) & 26(2)(ii) of the FSS Act, 2006 read with Section 3(1)(i) of the FSS Act, 2006, which is punishable u/s 54 of the FSS Act, 2006.
5. During the proceedings before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer, the appellant pleaded guilty.

Ld.
Adjudicating Officer taking into account the plea of guilt by the appellant held the appellant guilty and imposed the penalty.

6. The appellant has challenged the main the impugned order on the ground that the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer committed error by taking into account the confessional statement made by him.
It has been submitted that the appellant is a proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Sweets.
It has been submitted that in any case, the admission could not be considered to circumvent the provision of Section 26(2)(ii) of FSS Act, 2006.
It has been further submitted that the FSO did not mention in his complaint what was the strength and expiry date of the formalin.
The report of Food Analyst merely shows extraneous matter but no percentage of extraneous matter has been given.
The appellant has relied upon State (Delhi Administration) Vs. Janta South Masala Store & Ors., 2008 FAJ 542.

entities.text: State (Delhi Administration) Vs. Janta South Masala Store & Ors., 2008 FAJ 542
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been submitted that the penalty imposed upon the appellant is excessive in nature.
The appellant also submitted that in fact he was enforced to make confessional statement.
7. Notice of the appeal was issued to the respondent.
Sh. Kundan Lal, Ld. Chief PP for the respondent submitted that the sample was taken in accordance with the procedures in the presence of the appellant and the same was sent for the analysis.
Ld. Chief PP further submitted that opportunity was granted to the appellant to file an appeal against the report but he did not prefer.

Ld. Chief PP further submitted that it is proprietary item and the appellant has dully submitted that in "Rasbhari", there was Chhena, Sugar and Arrowroot and since extraneous matters have been found, the appellant is liable to be held guilty for violation of provision of Section 26(1) & 26(2)(ii) of the FSS Act, 2006 read with Section 3(1)(i) of the FSS Act, 2006, which is punishable u/s 54 of the FSS Act, 2006.

8. Section 54 of the FSS Act, 2006 reads as under:
"Penalty for food containing extraneous matter.

Any person whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption containing extraneous matter, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to one lakh rupees."
9.
I have considered the submissions.
I have gone through the handwritten statement made by the appellant before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer.

The scan copy of the handwritten statement made by the appellant is as under:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Perusal of the above statement would reveal that the appellant has made unconditional statement.
The judgments cited relate to prevention of food adulteration and I consider that the same are respectfully distinguished in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It is pertinent to take into account that in any case the punishment under the FSS Act, 2006 has been diluted to a large extent.
11. In view of the above discussions and in the facts and circumstances of the case, the appeal is dismissed.
12. TCR along with copy of the order be sent to the Ld. ADM, and thereafter appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
